title: Answering the new and releasing the old
meaning: Fresh understanding can guide your action when shared determination allows you to experience the ending of the earlier form.
text: Understanding that you want something different and feeling the end of the old are separate parts of a shared decision. Judgement in the physical position of Manipura describes action after reconsideration: returning to an important question and offering another answer. Judgement in energy identifies the motive, responding to an intention now heard more clearly. Death in emotions allows transition and the loss of an earlier form to be experienced. Judgement’s two roles distinguish renewed action from an inward call, while emotional completion can need time even when you both agree on the direction.

Imagine deciding to stop making a shared home calendar and preserve individual stories instead. The new approach interests you, yet sorting earlier drafts feels unexpectedly sad. **Agreement with change leaves room for feelings about what ends.** You can keep a few pages together and recognise the value of the earlier activity. That does not oblige you to resume it: a new decision can include appreciation of what came before.

The difficulty appears if fresh understanding must immediately cancel regret. A fond memory then seems like doubt about your choice, and sadness must be hidden. Change proceeds faster outwardly while openness diminishes. Completing an activity need not devalue its past. Naming what each leaves behind helps the decision remain shared throughout the transition, beyond the moment when you agreed to it.
